lines.text: Many learners say: Please close the gas before you leave.
Better: Please turn off the gas before you leave.
We turn off gas, water, and lights.
The second! Turn off the shower, please.

data.wrong: Please close the gas before you leave.
data.right: Please turn off the gas before you leave.
data.why: We turn off gas, water, and lights.

native.tip: Para gás, água ou luz, o inglês usa “turn off”, não “close”.

en.tip: For gas, water, or lights, English uses “turn off”, not “close”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “Please close the gas before you leave.” The right way is “Please turn off the gas before you leave.” In Portuguese we say “fechar o gás”, but in English it is “turn off the gas”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
